text:
dmitri: heads-up — oncall noticed a staging deploy to the gpu namespace started failing after yesterday's RBAC refactor. throwing forbidden errors from the apiserver. can we triage?
ben: saw the alert. putting logs here from the failing pod create attempt:
ben: `Warning  Failed     2m (x3 over 3m)  kubelet, gke-node  Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = permission denied`
elaine: error from kube-apiserver audit: `user="system:serviceaccount:ci:deploy" verb="create" resource="pods/exec" subresource="exec" namespace="gpu"` denied
carla: looks like the deploy SA lost exec/attach permissions when we tightened clusterrolebindings. we scoped a lot of verbs to reduce blast radius but missed a runtime path used by training jobs.
sec-incident-bot: incident-created id=SEC-2026-129 severity=low summary="deploy SA denied in gpu ns" assignee=@dmitri
dmitri: quick mitigation — can someone rebind the previous role for the gpu namespace so oncall can continue? we should do a safer rollback than a full clusterrole revert.
oncall-ops: rebind applied: `kubectl create rolebinding restore-deploy-binding --role=staging-deploy --serviceaccount=ci:deploy -n gpu` — confirmed pods now can start but still investigating exact permission set missing
ben: suggestion: create a narrow role for GPU workload lifecycle. only the minimal verbs the orchestrator needs. e.g. create/patch/get/list/watch on pods, but avoid granting full exec unless necessary. sample role:
ben: ```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: gpu-workload-lifecycle
  namespace: gpu
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "pods/status", "pods/log"]
  verbs: ["get", "create", "list", "watch", "patch"]
- apiGroups: ["apps"]
  resources: ["deployments"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "patch"]
```
elaine: we also need to check if the deploy pipeline uses `kubectl exec` for post-start hooks; if so, add `pods/exec` but gated to a new SA used only by those jobs. don't let the general deploy SA have exec.
carla: agreed. create `gpu-admin-runner-sa` for interactive ops with explicit annotation and short-lived tokens. map it in the CI step that needs exec only in canary stage.
dmitri: audit logging note — ensure kube-apiserver audit-policy captures requestObject and user info for these namespaces. we should have a dedicated audit rule for `gpu` to log non-resource requests and exec/attach.
ben: quick audit-rule snippet to add to audit-policy.yaml:
ben: ```yaml
- level: RequestResponse
  resources:
  - group: ""
    resources: ["pods/exec", "pods/attach"]
  namespaces: ["gpu"]
```
carla: KMS integration question — some secrets used by GPU workloads (runtime licenses) are encrypted with the cluster-level KMS provider. will a new SA need separate KMS permissions? we should avoid granting broad KMS usage.
elaine: yes — prefer using a KMS service account/key that is scoped to the namespace's SecretProviderClass (or CSI driver). that means creating a GCP/AWS IAM role for the CSI node plugin and only granting decrypt for those keys.
dmitri: for rollout plan:
- create namespace-local Role `gpu-workload-lifecycle` and RoleBinding for `ci:deploy` without exec
- introduce `gpu-admin-runner-sa` for exec needs and bind to that only in canary/ops
- add audit-policy rule for pods/exec and pods/attach in gpu ns
- update KMS IAM roles scoped to CSI usage, do not grant to deploy SA
- smoke tests: deploy small training pod, sleep, logs, and a canary that needs exec to verify separation
carla: vulnerability triage: while investigating, we found an old ClusterRoleBinding `legacy-editor` that still points to `system:serviceaccount:default:ci`. risk: broad edit perms. I propose removing that binding after migrating remaining workflows.
oncall-ops: noted. I created ticket SEC-2026-130 to track removing `legacy-editor` and enumerating dependent pipelines.
sec-incident-bot: sec ticket linked: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/SEC-2026-130
ben: tests to add to CI:
- RBAC integration test: simulate serviceaccount token and attempt all verbs against pods/deployments in gpu ns
- KMS decrypt test using restricted role credentials
- audit log assertion: that exec/attach requests are logged
dmitri: timeline — want the minimal role + binding and audit rule in staging by EOD, canary tomorrow to prod if green. please @carla @ben coordinate changes and PRs. label PRs `security/rbac-gpu`
elaine: I'll own the KMS IAM changes and the CSI mapping. will open PR with docs on key scoping.
carla: opening RBAC PR now, will include the tests described. pinging #eng-ci for runner setup.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline run started for PR #4621 — status: queued
ben: thanks all. once PR merges let's run verification checklist and close SEC-2026-129. also schedule a short postmortem to capture why the permission matrix changed unexpectedly.
dmitri: good call. add retrospective notes to the ticket and let's ensure role-change PRs include a simple `rbac-impact` checklist that triggers a manual review for runtime-critical namespaces.
elaine: one more: add a monitoring alert for sudden drops in `pods created` success rate per namespace for 5m window so this class of regression gets caught earlier.
carla: added to monitoring playbook.
oncall-ops: all clear from oncall's side now, will keep watch for 2 hours.
sec-incident-bot: incident SEC-2026-129 status: mitigated, monitoring for regression
